abstract.text:
Occlusion relationship reasoning based on convolution
neural networks consists of two subtasks: occlusion boundary extraction and occlusion orientation inference. Due to
the essential differences between the two subtasks in the feature expression at the higher and lower stages, it is challenging to carry on them simultaneously in one network. To
address this issue, we propose a novel Dual-path Decoder
Network, which uniformly extracts occlusion information
at higher stages and separates into two paths to recover
boundary and occlusion orientation respectively in lower
stages. Besides, considering the restriction of occlusion orientation presentation to occlusion orientation learning, we
design a new orthogonal representation for occlusion orientation and proposed the Orthogonal Orientation Regression
loss which can get rid of the unfitness between occlusion
representation and learning and further prompt the occlusion orientation learning. Finally, we apply a multi-scale
loss together with our proposed orientation regression loss
to guide the boundary and orientation path learning respectively. Experiments demonstrate that our proposed method
achieves state-of-the-art results on PIOD and BSDS ownership datasets.

abstract.text:
Occlusion relationship reasoning based on convolution
neural networks consists of two subtasks: occlusion boundary extraction and occlusion orientation inference. Due to
the essential differences between the two subtasks in the feature expression at the higher and lower stages, it is challenging to carry on them simultaneously in one network. To
address this issue, we propose a novel Dual-path Decoder
Network, which uniformly extracts occlusion information
at higher stages and separates into two paths to recover
boundary and occlusion orientation respectively in lower
stages. Besides, considering the restriction of occlusion orientation presentation to occlusion orientation learning, we
design a new orthogonal representation for occlusion orientation and proposed the Orthogonal Orientation Regression
loss which can get rid of the unfitness between occlusion
representation and learning and further prompt the occlusion orientation learning. Finally, we apply a multi-scale
loss together with our proposed orientation regression loss
to guide the boundary and orientation path learning respectively. Experiments demonstrate that our proposed method
achieves state-of-the-art results on PIOD and BSDS ownership datasets.

relations.quote: DOC [19] uses two networks for occlusion boundary pixel classification and occlusion orientation regression respectively.
relations.why: The paper builds on DOC's task formulation but criticizes its separate-network and continuous-orientation approach.

relations.quote: DOOBNet [18] designs an unified end-to-end multi-task deep object occlusion boundary detection network to simultaneously predict object boundary and occlusion orientation by sharing convolutional features.
relations.why: DOOBNet shares an entire decoder, while DDNet argues for sharing only higher stages and splitting lower stages.

relations.quote: OFNet [10] considers the importance of occlusion cues for two tasks, and designs two sub-networks to share occlusion cues.
relations.why: OFNet's two-subnetwork design is a direct predecessor and baseline for DDNet's dual-path decoder.

relations.quote: Experiments prove that we achieve state-of-the-art results on both PIOD [19] and BSDS ownership [13] datasets.

supercut.text: The paper starts from the two subtasks of occlusion relationship reasoning and argues that they differ in what they need from CNN features.
The occlusion information extracted from higher stages is consistent for both tasks, while lower stages tend to contain more specific spatial information that two tasks prefer respectively.
To address two issues, we propose a novel path-splitting decoder structure for predicting boundary and occlusion orientation, called the Dual-path Decoder Network (DDNet).
The decoder shares high-stage occlusion information and then separates into a boundary path and an orientation path for lower stages.
Furthermore, to make full use of multi-scale features and spatial information, we design a multi-scale supervision method for boundary path.
We define a new orthogonal occlusion orientation representation, which decomposes the orientation orthogonally into a horizontal vector ~a = (a, 0) and a vertical vector ~b = (0, b) as the Fig. 4.
Based on our representation, we proposed a novel loss called Orthogonal Orientation Regression loss
The orientation loss avoids the periodicity problem by learning normalized orthogonal vectors, while boundary training uses a class-balanced cross-entropy with multi-scale side supervision.
The best results appear when sharing the top-2 stages, which is also the structure we use.
